history.summary: A 23-year-old large 1,356 sqft 3BR in Bukit Batok, 460m from Bukit Gombak MRT, asking just $1,106 PSF — a ~10% discount to the $1,228 median — at a low $1.5M absolute. Genuine value (cheap PSF, deep buyer band, near-MRT, 5.9% CAGR), but the age (~77yr lease left), OCR-west location with limited catalysts, and a thinner 71-txn sample temper it to a Buy with the value real but the growth ceiling modest.
history.rating_rationale: Real value play: $1,106 PSF is a ~10% discount to the $1,228 median on a large 1,356 sqft unit, and the $1.5M absolute sits in the deepest buyer band — exactly the affordability profile that resells easily to HDB upgraders. 460m to Bukit Gombak MRT (NSL) gives solid connectivity, 5.9% URA resale CAGR over 71 txns is healthy, ~3.4% yield is among the better in the batch, and score 692 / MMR 1532 is respectable. Held to a plain Buy by the 2003 build (~77yr lease, ageing finishes), the mature D23 west location with no major near-term catalyst (no new MRT line, no govt transformation zone within reach), and a moderate 71-transaction sample. Solid, affordable, fairly-bought — but the upside is steady rather than catalytic.

history.summary: Large 1,356 sqft 3BR in Bukit Batok (D23/OCR) at $1,106 psf, genuinely a touch below the project's recent average, but on a 23-year-old 99-LH where lease decay is the dominant risk over a 5-7yr hold.
history.rating_rationale: The asking $1,106 psf is mildly below the project's verified last-12-month average ($1,180-$1,200 psf; range $911-$1,260), and the -8.7% psf_premium rests on a reasonable 16-txn cohort, so the discount is real but modest - consistent with a large 3BR's natural PSF compression rather than a deep bargain. OCR is the best forward region (~+4.0%). The decisive offset is age: built 2003 on a 99-LH from 2000 means only ~77 years remaining, and over a 5-7yr hold the asset crosses further into the zone where lease-decay drag and CPF-usage/financing tightening compress buyer demand. Location is decent (Bukit Batok / near Bukit Gombak) but no fresh dated catalyst. Net: a fairly priced large unit whose age caps the forward upside to roughly market - a genuine near-tie that lands Neutral.

history.summary: A genuine 1,356 sqft 3BR at The Madeira (D23 Bukit Batok, 99LH from 2000, 73yr left) asking $1.50M / $1,106 psf. The algo's 787 score rests on a discount that does not survive inspection: against the project's OWN low-floor prints in the same size band the ask is -1.8% (i.e. at market), and the -14.5% 'vs district peers' is the D23 Hillview-vs-Bukit-Batok sub-market gap, not value. Fairly priced, not cheap.
history.rating_rationale: Not a bargain, and not a trap either — an at-market purchase of the softest format in the project. Two independent checks dissolve the discount. (1) FLOOR ARTIFACT: The Madeira has a clean 8.6% floor gradient in the 1,261-1,451 sqft band over 36mo (floors 01-10 median $1,126 psf, n=7; floors 16+ median $1,222, n=6; 28 storeys total). The $1,106 ask sits -1.8% from the low-floor median and -9.5% from the high-floor median — it is priced as a low-floor unit because it almost certainly is one. MMR's two largest positive components, age_value +10.98 and psf_value +4.45 (~36% of its entire margin over base 1500), are crediting that gradient as value. The v3.12 low-floor defences never fired: no researched stack profile and no floor_level on the record, so stack_low_floor_share and the low_floor component both sat at 0.0 — the defence was ABSENT, not passed. (2) SUB-MARKET LEVEL, NOT VALUE: D23 is two price worlds. In this size band over 24mo, Hillview/Dairy Farm projects median $1,641 psf vs Bukit Batok/Gombak $1,212 and Choa Chu Kang $1,139. The Madeira's own $1,212 median puts it at the TOP of its real Bukit Batok/CCK peer set (above Parkview $983, Regent Grove $1,000, Palm Gardens $1,059, Regent Heights $1,089, Northvale $1,100, Mayspings $1,147, The Warren $1,178, Hillview Regency $1,194). It is the expensive end of the cheap belt, not cheap. (3) THE LIVE BOOK AGREES: this exact 1,356 sqft / $1.50M / $1,106 psf ask has stood since 2026-06-07 (~8 weeks), relisted through three different agents (60128058 -> 60135268 -> 500190637, addresses #50 and #52), and is below PropertyGuru's own stated live range for the project ($1,162-$1,282 psf). A genuinely underpriced large 3BR at the deepest quantum band in a 456-unit project does not sit unsold for two months at an unchanged price. What holds up: the bedroom count is REAL (bed_bands 'ok' vs a 122-contract URA rental band — this is not a relabelled 2BR+study, which is what usually kills these), the trailing CAGR is NOT a size-mix artifact (decomposed: every size band ~7-9% over the window with stable median sqft 1243->1270->1248), and the downside record is genuinely strong (87.4% of 350 resales profitable, a sample well past any trust threshold). Against that: 1.99% NET yield is thin carry with no compensation, large-format momentum is the project's weakest segment (last two 1,300-1,450 prints: Nov-25 $1,080, Feb-26 $1,052; momentum -0.92), 73yr lease exits at 66-68yr into a narrowing CPF/financing pool, and the nearest catalyst (Tengah JRL) is 2.39km away and carries no measured forward power anyway. Net: pay market price for an ageing leasehold large unit in the softest slice of its own project. That is a Neutral, and the 787 score should NOT put it at the top of a shortlist. It only becomes interesting if the floor is verified at 11+ (then $1,106 psf really is ~9% under its true comp) or the ask breaks below ~$1.42M.

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: $4,250/mo from 28 URA project-bed contracts (confidence 0.95) = 3.4% gross, 1.99% net. Independently corroborated by EdgeProp's $3.4 psf pm average for the project (implying ~$4,610 on 1,356 sqft, range $4,068-5,560), so the estimate is sound-to-slightly-conservative. No yield artifact here — but 1.99% net is thin carry that does not pay you to wait, and large units rent at the bottom of the project's psf-pm range.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: Trailing 5.92%/yr (URA 5yr CAGR, 71 txns) is real within-project growth, not a size-mix artifact — I decomposed it by size band (<1000: ~8.1%, 1150-1300: ~9.0%, 1300-1450: ~7.0%) with a stable median size across periods (1243 -> 1270 -> 1248 sqft). But it is a single 2021-26 bull-regime read and trailing CAGR has ~0 measured forward power. Forward, I mark it down to the OCR baseline with a haircut: the large-format segment this unit sits in is the project's weakest (Nov-25 $1,080, Feb-26 $1,052 prints), momentum is -0.92, and the lease runs into a narrower buyer pool at exit. Override to 3.5%/yr.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: No researched profile for The Madeira (status: not_researched), so no stack/facing join was possible — and that absence is material here, because it is why the low-floor defences did not fire. Inferred from URA prints instead: 28 storeys, and the 1,261-1,451 sqft band shows a monotone floor gradient (01-05 $1,095, 06-10 $1,143, 11-15 $1,217, 16-20 $1,222, 21-25 $1,217). The $1,106 ask lands in the 01-10 zone. Before any offer, verify the actual floor — that single fact flips this between 'at market' and 'genuinely ~9% under comp'. Running /research-development on The Madeira would make this join real rather than inferred.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_rate_source: OCR realized forward baseline from the repo's own 28-district backtest (+3.7%/yr), haircut for negative large-format momentum (-0.92; last two 1,300-1,450 sqft prints $1,080 and $1,052) and lease decay into the exit. Trailing 5.92% URA CAGR deliberately NOT used forward — resale-to-resale verified as real but single-regime, and trailing CAGR carries ~0 forward power per v3.5 priors.
